name: Break the Sequential Dependency of LLM Inference Using Lookahead Decoding
problem: Speculative decoding requires an auxiliary draft MODEL or a data store, which is nontrivial to obtain, cannot generalise, and adds memory and engineering cost.
mechanism: EXACT parallel decoding with no auxiliary model and no data store. Runs an n-gram pool of (K, V) verification branches in parallel, each computing an N-gram Prediction (NgramPool) of possible next tokens from a 2D window of preceding tokens plus the branch's own history; a Jacobi iteration maps each candidate branch to a token deterministically from the target model's logits. Branches that agree with the Jacobi trajectory are accepted - because the map is a deterministic function of logits, acceptance is exact and the output distribution is unchanged. Explicitly trades per-step log(FLOPs) for a smaller number of total decoding steps, and is compatible with concurrent memory-efficient attention (FlashAttention).
speedup_reported: Up to 1.8x on MT-bench and up to 4x with STRONG SCALING ON MULTIPLE GPUs on code completion. The 4x is a multi-GPU scaling number, not a single-accelerator result - a critical distinction, because the whole premise is that decoding underutilises a single device's compute. Baseline is plain autoregressive decoding.
notes: ADOPTION, precisely: llama.cpp and TensorRT-LLM both ship a lookahead-decoding path, and vLLM has supported it. The distinct selling point versus every other record in this sub-area is that it needs NO draft model and NO draft weights, so it applies to any checkpoint unmodified - the reason it survived when many paper-specific draft methods did not. HEADLINE-CLAIM TRAP, flagged deliberately: the 4x figure requires strong scaling across multiple GPUs. Quote the 1.8x single-device number for any single-accelerator comparison and say so explicitly, or this paper will be cited as evidence that lookahead decoding gives 4x on a single GPU, which it does not.
